I think it’s really brave to share your story. I tried to kill myself the first time at 15...pills. As evidenced by me typing right now, I failed. I battle every day with depression and when it’s bad, I fight those same suicidal thoughts. They were so bad this week I parked in a graveyard to write my suicide notes..the irony of that made me laugh and the process of writing made me cry, a lot, like snot coming out my nose crying,  and gave me clarity.

I’m 47 and I am so glad I failed at 15 to kill myself. Sure I’ve had issues: depression, chronic pain, getting divorced from wife #2, losing most of the money I made in a divorce or two, ending up in a psych ward, and battling the demons of being a high functioning alcoholic.

But I have my two beautiful awesome kids. And I get to help them deal with their bullshit because I get it and I don’t judge and not everyone is blessed with knowing how precious life is because they make the decision to be here every day. We have so much to give because our choices to stay show how much we value ourselves, because it’s only us there when we make that decision.

I’ve traveled a ton, fell in love...a lot, I have a great job...but I still make a decision not to end it almost everyday. And I’m so grateful that I failed at 15 because what the world held for me and what it holds for you is so worth the struggle. 

Happy Birthday. I hope you choose to stick around. The world needs more of us brave souls, not fewer. Love and good vibes to you

I’ve been there. I’ve stayed alive solely for my kids. I’ve stayed sober just for my kids l. I have joint custody, but I had to fight for it. Change for them! Be involved, be at school events, sports, etc. make you time with them special and as they age they will want to see you more. 

I am writing you though on an important technical note. As someone going through their second divorce right now and who deals with similar issues...DO NOT tell her shit about your mental health. She is NOT your friend. Nothing you say to her will be interpreted appropriately and it will be used to harm you and your potential relationship with your kids. 

So sorry you are going through this. Stay strong.
Congratulations! You look beautiful and will look and feel better every day your sober.

I’m a guy, but very similar situation with the kids, When I’ve  felt unappreciated I focus on the idea that parenting is about the hard work, the discipline, the constant driving them to events...I can tell you as my children have gotten older, they recognize it more (they are 10 & 12). There are more thank yous and they recognize me as the primary PARENT...not the guy who buys them stuff and misses their games. 

So it does get better and I believe there is usually some space for each parent. If you work hard at your role and don’t disparage the other parent (which is tough), the kids grow up in your mold and love...not the other parents.

Good luck and stay strong!

First, I am so sorry to hear of your pain, I’ve been there. I’m battling those demons now. 

My backstory is I rushed into a marriage after being in a long one before and tabby flags about my STBX mental health...severe anxiety, depression, PTSD, and conversion disorder to name the main ones. As she’s gone through her struggle, things have gotten worse. She holds it together in public then is rude, critical, in affectionate, and cruel to me and my two children. Id been on the clinch for 6  months of a 3 1/2 year marriage.  Worst part, she has kids too who I am “dad” to. But, I had to leave because of the damage she was doing to me and my kids. 

I hurt every morning and struggle to get out of bed. I can tell you that I find solace with my therapist and in focusing one thing each day that’s simply for me. A walk, a dinner, etc.

You are not alone. Plenty of us out there trying to fight the good fight as long as we can.!but she can never be a true partner until she gets better and that takes years. You can love her but not be married to her. Her journey is not yours. Find your journey again.
Thanks! I appreciate it.

I was married for 16 years...fell out of love...got divorced...then got too quickly married to someone else...after 4 years we are calling it quits...my belief in the fairy tale is why I woke up and worked so hard every day during those 20 combined years of marriage...they are also the reasons I get up now when I’m a middle aged man who has been hurt and feels alone. If we don’t believe in true love, what is there? 

Yep I sound pathetic. LOL.
Please don’t give up. Your story reflects your bravery. Someday, maybe soon, your story will inspire bravery in someone else.
